sources.entry: optuna - A hyperparameter optimization framework with define-by-run search spaces and pruning of unpromising trials.

summary.one_liner: Optuna is a Python framework for automatic hyperparameter optimization with a define-by-run API, letting users build search spaces dynamically in ordinary Python code.
summary.what_it_does: Users write an objective function that calls trial.suggest_* methods to sample hyperparameters, and Optuna runs many trials to find the best values. Search spaces can include conditionals and loops because they are defined in normal Python. The README describes state-of-the-art sampling and pruning of unpromising trials, and parallel scaling to many workers with few code changes. Studies can persist to a database such as SQLite, and the optuna-dashboard package provides a real-time web UI for optimization history and hyperparameter importance. The README also covers an experimental Rust reimplementation called Rustuna and OptunaHub, a platform for sharing registered samplers and features.
use_cases: tune hyperparameters of a scikit-learn model
search machine learning model settings automatically
run distributed hyperparameter searches across workers
visualize optimization history and parameter importance
how_to_run: Write an objective(trial) function using trial.suggest_* calls
notable: Define-by-run API: search spaces are built dynamically with normal Python conditionals and loops
Pruning of unpromising trials to save compute
Optuna Dashboard web UI for live study inspection
OptunaHub for loading community samplers and features
Rustuna, an experimental Rust implementation with faster samplers and zero Python runtime dependencies
caveats: Rustuna is experimental and lacks some Optuna features and APIs
OptunaHub AutoSampler needs extra dependencies such as PyTorch
